title: Find the bug in a title_case function
prompt:
This function is supposed to capitalize the first letter of every word in a sentence but only capitalizes the very first word. Assume the input is lowercase words separated by single spaces (no apostrophes or punctuation).

def title_case(s):
    return s[0].upper() + s[1:]

Identify the bug, explain the fix, and provide the corrected function in a fenced Python code block (starting with ```python), keeping the name and signature `title_case(s)`.

metadata.notes: Bug: only touches the first character of the whole string, not each word. Fix should split on spaces, capitalize each word, and rejoin. Revised (2026-09-23, V2.6 Phase 1): prompt now pins the input shape (lowercase, single-space-separated, no punctuation) to avoid the apostrophe/str.title() edge case the original notes flagged as ambiguous, and requests a fenced code block for the sandboxed grader; bug/difficulty unchanged.
